text:
Sanjay: Heads-up, bringing orca-lite-3b (q4f) into the eval harness and hitting a weird failure.
Sanjay: On SQuAD-like runs factuality_score drops from ~0.72 -> 0.18 after quant. Runner then emits NaN in metric_aggregator and CI job 4521 fails.
Marta: ugh. Any logs? stack trace?
Sanjay: Paste of final lines from runner:
```
2026-03-18T12:34:21Z runner ERROR metric_aggregator: value error computing mean: NaN encountered
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/eval/runner/metrics.py", line 128, in aggregate
    return np.nanmean(values)
  File "<__array_function__ internals>", line 6, in nanmean
ValueError: All-NaN slice
```
Sanjay: Also see a lot of empty strings returned from decoder for some examples.
Devon: Empty tokens -> could be tokenizer issue. Did tokenization/normalize_unicodes run? Orca tokenizers sometimes preserve ZWJ/ZWSP sequences.
Lin: We saw a similar perf earlier where zero-width joiners made some targets empty after detokenize. Try running: `python -m eval_tooling.normalize --model-config models/orca-lite3b.json --strip-zero-width` to test.
Sanjay: Ran that locally, helps some examples but still many NaNs in metric aggregation. CI job shows more failures than my local run (env difference?).
ci-bot: CI job 4521 failed for branch `onboard/orca-lite3b-quant` — test/eval-runner::integration (see https://ci.redwood.example/4521)
Marta: CI difference likely from metrics package version. Which metrics lib is CI using vs local venv?
Sanjay: Local: redwood-metrics 0.9.1. CI image uses 0.9.0 (ugh). Dev dep pinned in dockerfile.
Devon: 0.9.1 fixed a regression where empty-string predictions were filtered incorrectly; 0.9.0 returned empty token arrays which metric code didn't handle -> All-NaN when computing means.
Alex: Quick patch options: (A) upgrade metrics package in CI image to 0.9.1, (B) add defensive filtering in eval-runner aggregate to drop non-finite and empty predictions, (C) canonicalize detokenize to return at least empty-string placeholder. I'd do both A+B.
Lin: For the tokenizer side, I recommend adding a `strip_unicode` flag to the model config so onboarding can opt-in to drop invisible separators (helpful for Orca family). Example patch to models/orca-lite3b.json:
```
{
  "model": "orca-lite3b",
  "quant": "q4f",
  "tokenizer": {
    "type": "hf-bpe",
    "normalize_unicodes": true,
    "strip_zero_width": true
  }
}
```
Marta: Can you open a tiny PR for that config change and link to CI job? I'll sign off.
Sanjay: Created PR #834 (onboard/orca-lite3b-tokenizer-config) with two commits: add strip_zero_width flag + test vector for the example that was empty. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/834
Sanjay: Also filed issue for metrics pinning in our base images: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/issues/1294
Devon: I'm pushing a tiny hotfix to eval-runner to be defensive (PR #835). Patch diff (core):
```
- values = np.array(vals)
- return np.nanmean(values)
+ values = np.array([v for v in vals if (v is not None) and (not (isinstance(v, str) and v == ""))])
+ if values.size == 0:
+     return float('nan')
+ return np.nanmean(values)
```
Alex: I'll update the CI dockerfile in infra (upgrade redwood-metrics to 0.9.1) and kick a rebuild. ETA ~30m.
ci-bot: Docker build started for infra/ci-image (build 2103) by Alex.
Marta: Once CI image is updated and PRs #834 and #835 land we should re-run job 4521 and also run a full eval sweep on the canary subset (10k queries) to verify no silent regressions.
Sanjay: Agreed. One more gotcha: quant q4f randomness makes tokenization boundaries more brittle; I'll add a small deterministic seed in the ONBOARD workflow to reduce variance while we validate.
Lin: For the dashboard: add a metric panel to show percent_empty_predictions per model/version so future onboards show this signal early.
Alex: noted, filing dashboard task.
Sanjay: Thanks all — I'll watch the PRs and re-run CI once Alex's image is ready. :thumbsup:
Marta: TY!
